ANIMAL & HABITAT WORKSHEETS · AGES 4–5

Animals & Their Habitats worksheets — printables for little hands.

Six genuine habitat sheets, one for each big home: the desert, the farm, the forest, the ocean, the polar regions and the wetland. On every sheet your child circles who lives there, matches each animal to its home, counts, chooses the right scene and traces the habitat word. Download the original sheet, print it, or solve every sheet on screen in Class 36 first.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Desert Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A desert animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle who really lives in the desert, match camel, fennec fox and lizard to their desert homes, count cacti and trace the word DESERT. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/desert-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Three of the five animals live in the desert — circle them.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each desert animal to its desert home: the rocks, the dunes or the burrow.

  3. 3

    Count

    One group has exactly 3 cacti — count each group and circle the right one.

  4. 4

    Choose

    Two scenes, one desert — circle the sandy one.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the big word DESERT, then try it on your own.

Before you start, have the words ready: The word desert, and three desert residents your child can name on sight: camel, fennec fox and lizard.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The desert is hot and dry, and the animals that live there are built for it — padded feet, big ears, burrows under the sand.

Saying who does NOT belong is the fast route to understanding who does — the penguin and the bear make the desert definition sharp.

  • Habitat vocabulary
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Matching animals to homes
  • Counting to 4
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The desert is the hottest, driest home on the sheet — let us find the animals who can take the heat.

Questions to ask: Could the penguin live here? Why not? What would the camel say about all that ice?

Parent tips: Sand in a tray plus a toy camel turns the matching row into a small world after the sheet is done.

Home practice: On a hot sunny walk, ask: who is the camel of our neighborhood today?

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Farm Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A farm animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the animals that live on a farm, match each one to its barn, stable, pen or sty, count the hay and trace the word FARM. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/farm-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Four of these five animals live on a farm — circle the whole farm team.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from each animal to its home: the barn, the sty, the stable and the pen.

  3. 3

    Count

    Count the hay bales in each group and circle the group with exactly 4.

  4. 4

    Choose

    One scene is the farm — circle it and name what you see in it.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the word FARM, then write it yourself in the box.

Before you start, have the words ready: The farm team — cow, horse, pig, hen and sheep — and the word farm for the place they all live.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

A farm is a habitat people built: every animal on it has a home with a name — barn, sty, coop, pen.

The farm is usually a child's first habitat with names for the homes themselves, which plants the idea that where you live has a word.

  • Farm animal names
  • Home vocabulary: barn, sty, coop, pen
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Counting to 5
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The farm is the one habitat with a barn in it. Let us get every animal home before supper.

Questions to ask: Who sleeps in the barn? Who loves the mud? Which animal on this sheet have you seen for real?

Parent tips: After the sheet, line up toy farm animals and build each home from blocks — the words come out on their own.

Home practice: Visit a farm or a petting zoo and find one home from the sheet in real life — barns count double.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Forest Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A forest animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle who lives in the forest, match squirrel, bear and deer to their forest homes, count the trees and trace the word FOREST. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/forest-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Three of the five animals live in the forest — circle the forest friends.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from squirrel, bear and deer to the tree hollow, the cave and the bush.

  3. 3

    Count

    One group has exactly 4 trees — count each row and circle it.

  4. 4

    Choose

    Two scenes — circle the one that shows the forest.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the big word FOREST, letter by letter, then write it once.

Before you start, have the words ready: The word forest, and three forest neighbors — squirrel, bear and deer — plus the fox who lives there too.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The forest is a home you can walk under: tall trees give food, shade and hiding places, and every forest animal uses them its own way.

Forests are the habitat children meet in storybooks first; naming its residents turns familiar pictures into real knowledge.

  • Habitat vocabulary
  • Matching animals to homes
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Counting to 5
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Under the tall trees lives a whole neighborhood — let us meet who hides in the forest.

Questions to ask: Who stores food in a tree? Who sleeps all winter? Where would you hide if you were small and furry?

Parent tips: On the next walk under trees, play spot-the-home: holes, nests, burrows all count.

Home practice: Collect one fallen leaf on your next walk and call it forest mail — delivered to the fridge.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Ocean Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A ocean animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the ocean animals, match the whale, clownfish and sea turtle to the reef, the open sea and the seabed, count the fish and trace the word OCEAN. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/ocean-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Three of the five animals live in the ocean — circle the swimmers.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from whale, clownfish and turtle to the open sea, the coral reef and the seabed.

  3. 3

    Count

    Count the fish in each group and circle the group with exactly 5.

  4. 4

    Choose

    One picture is the ocean — circle it and name one thing that lives there.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the big word OCEAN, then write it in the box.

Before you start, have the words ready: The word ocean, and three ocean residents on the sheet: whale, clownfish and sea turtle.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The ocean is the biggest habitat on Earth — and even inside it, animals split it up: the reef, the open water, the sandy floor.

Splitting one huge habitat into addresses — reef, open sea, seabed — is the first step from "fish live in water" to real ecology.

  • Habitat vocabulary
  • Matching animals to ocean homes
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Counting to 6
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The ocean is one home so big it has rooms inside it — let us find who lives where.

Questions to ask: Who breathes air but lives in the sea? (The whale — a real surprise.) Who paints the reef orange?

Parent tips: A bathtub becomes the open sea, a sponge the reef — retell the matching row with bath toys.

Home practice: At bath time or a aquarium visit, use the three ocean words: reef, open sea, seabed.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Polar Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A polar animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the polar animals, match the polar bear, penguin and arctic fox to the ice floe, the icebergs and the snowy hills, count ice blocks and trace the word POLAR. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/polar-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Three of the five animals love the ice — circle the polar team.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from polar bear, penguin and arctic fox to the ice floe, the icebergs and the snowy hills.

  3. 3

    Count

    Count the ice blocks in each group and circle the group with exactly 4.

  4. 4

    Choose

    Two scenes, one frozen — circle the polar habitat.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the big word POLAR, then write it on your own.

Before you start, have the words ready: The word polar, and three ice-ready residents: polar bear, penguin and arctic fox.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

The polar regions are the coldest habitats on Earth, and their animals wear built-in coats — thick fur or a layer of fat.

Extreme habitats make the matching rule obvious: nobody survives the ice without the right equipment, and the sheet shows exactly whose bodies have it.

  • Habitat vocabulary
  • Matching animals to icy homes
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Counting to 5
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: The coldest homes on Earth belong to the warmest-dressed animals — let us meet the polar team.

Questions to ask: What do polar bears and penguins both wear that we have to zip on? Who slides on their tummy?

Parent tips: Freeze a small bowl of water, slide the toy penguin on top, and the floe word becomes real.

Home practice: Next snowy or cold day, one minute of penguin walking — wings in, tiny steps, the word polar said twice.

WORKSHEET · CLASS 36 · AGES 4–5

Wetland Animals and Their Habitat Worksheet for Ages 4–5

A wetland animals worksheet for ages 4–5: circle the wetland animals, match the frog, egret and crocodile to the pond, the reeds and the burrow, count lily pads and trace the word WETLAND. Printable.

Download the sheet

Teaching tips
THE WORKSHEET

The full sheet, exactly as the artist drew it.

See the whole sheet, download the original file or print it from your browser. Want your child to solve it on screen first? The interactive version lives at preschool/4-years/animals-and-their-habitats/worksheets/wetland-animals-and-their-habitat/ / — same sheet, drawing layer included.

HOW TO USE IT

The five steps on the sheet.

  1. 1

    Circle

    Four of the five animals live in the wetland — circle the whole soggy team.

  2. 2

    Match

    Draw a line from frog, egret and crocodile to the lily pond, the reedy bank and the mud burrow.

  3. 3

    Count

    One group has exactly 4 lily pads — count each group and circle it.

  4. 4

    Choose

    Two scenes — circle the one that shows the wetland.

  5. 5

    Trace

    Trace the big word WETLAND, then write it in the box.

Before you start, have the words ready: The word wetland, and three wetland regulars on the sheet: frog, egret and crocodile.

WHY IT HELPS

What this worksheet teaches.

A wetland is land that is soaked — ponds, reeds and mud — and it is a dinner, a bath and a hiding place all at once.

The wetland is the habitat that is neither dry nor deep — naming it teaches children that habitats come in every in-between flavor, not just desert versus ocean.

  • Habitat vocabulary
  • Matching animals to wetland homes
  • Sorting belong and not belong
  • Counting to 4
  • Word tracing
FOR GROWN-UPS

Tips, questions and practice.

Say before you start: Where the water meets the grass, the wetland squelches — let us find who loves it that way.

Questions to ask: Who hops and who wades? What does the crocodile use the mud for? Have you ever heard frogs at night?

Parent tips: After the sheet, jump like a frog, wade slowly like an egret and snap like a crocodile — three animals, three moves.

Home practice: Pass any pond or canal on your walks and ask: who from our sheet could live here?
